  "text": "By morning, the narrow passage was gone. Ada walked the length of the street twice, counting the houses between the bakery and the school. There were six, as there had always been, and no gap wide enough for a gate.

The constable met her outside the bakery. He had brought the key in an envelope, though he would not say why. When Ada tipped it into her palm, she found a small brass button.

“That was on her coat,” he said.

Ada closed her fingers around it. The child’s coat had been blue, with mismatched buttons. She remembered sewing this one on by candlelight, the winter before the letters began.

Inside the bakery, the ovens were cold. The baker stood behind the counter reading an envelope addressed in a careful, slanting hand. He looked up when Ada entered.

“It came under the door,” he said. “There’s one for you.”

The envelope was damp but unsealed. Ada drew out a single sheet. On it was a drawing of the little brick house, its garden neat, its upstairs window open. Three figures stood at the front door. One was a child in a blue coat. Another was the woman. The third had been sketched so faintly that Ada had to turn the page toward the window.

It was herself.

Below the drawing, in the same careful hand, someone had written: Thank you for showing us the way.

Ada folded the sheet. Outside, the constable was staring across the street. Between the houses, a gate stood open."
